newsitem.title: USA: New York 7-year-old in sexual harassment flap.
newsitem.headline: New York 7-year-old in sexual harassment flap.

text.p: Just 10 days after a 6-year-old North Carolina boy was suspended from school for kissing a girl on the cheek, a 7-year-old New York boy suffered a similar fate but had his suspension lifted on Wednesday.

Education officials said De'Andre Dearinge, who was suspended for five days this week on a charge of sexual harassment after he kissed a classmate and pulled a button off her skirt at a public school in Queens, would be able to return to school on Thursday.

"The principal made the decision based on the facts that she had at the moment and possibly the use with a 7-year-old of the term 'sexual harassment' was inappropriate but certainly the behaviour dictated a closer look at what the child did," the school's deputy superintendant Kenneth Grover told reporters.

The New York Daily News reported that the boy admitted to his mother he had kissed the girl "because I like her" and had taken the button because his favourite book is "Corduroy" about a bear with a missing button.

The school district follows board guidelines that define sexual harassment as sexually suggestive comments, innuendos or propositions or inappropriate physical contact of a sexual nature, such as touching, patting or pinching.

In Lexington, North Carolina, 6-year-old Jonathan Prevette was suspended for a day from school last month after he kissed a girl on the cheek. The child subsequently appeared on several television and radio talk shows.
